title: Counit-normalized adjoint transport through equivalences
statement: Let C,D,C′,D′ be categories, E:C→C′ and H:D→D′ equivalences, F:C→D left adjoint to R, and F′:C′→D′ left adjoint to G. Given b:F⋙H≅E⋙F′, there is a unique rho:R⋙E≅H⋙G satisfying b_RL followed by F′(rho_L) and the second counit equals H of the first counit. For every v:F(M)→L, E of its first transpose followed by rho equals the second transpose of b_M inverse followed by H(v).

source.place: Proof (3), finite-ring tensor formula; explicit site transport steps of lem-pur-finite-ring-site-tensor-transpose

proof.text: Define the natural mate by the second adjunction Hom equivalence applied to b inverse followed by the first counit. Naturality is the square and counit naturality.

Postcomposition by each mate component is a composite of full-faithfulness Hom bijections, the two adjunctions and b. Essential surjectivity of E extends this bijectivity to all test objects; Yoneda gives invertibility. The inverse Hom equivalence proves the counit equation and uniqueness. Applying it once more proves the transpose identity. These steps are fully proved in Lean.
